idiom_name: Optional with optional chaining / if-let binding and compactMap
implementation_notes: Swift's Optional is a first-class enum with language support: postfix optional chaining short-circuits a whole chain to nil, if let/guard let bind the absent case away and ?? supplies a default, so the 0..1 focus is part of the type system. The plural traversal is Sequence's compactMap, which keeps only the non-nil results of a transform, and flatMap, which flattens one level of nesting; these replace the classic optic structure. Optional chaining is the idiom for a single path, while an optics library is only needed for composed, reusable focus paths.
pitfalls: The result of an optional chain is always optional, even when the property is not; force-unwrapping it with ! crashes when any link was nil.
compactMap silently drops nil results, so a legitimate nil in the data disappears from the result.
Implicitly unwrapped optionals postpone the crash instead of handling absence; they express lifecycle guarantees, not optional domain data.
